subject.title: Unhandled Playwright assertion error in CRSession._onMessage crashes Gateway

question: Should OpenClaw handle this CRSession CDP assertion by narrow browser-owned classification/quarantine, by a larger browser subprocess isolation boundary, or by waiting for fresh live proof before implementation?
rationale: Source shows the fatal path remains, but the durable fix changes how much unknown Playwright/CDP state Gateway should suppress versus isolate, which is a maintainer reliability policy choice.

options.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
options.body: Keep this issue open while a browser/Gateway owner defines profile quarantine or subprocess isolation semantics and the live proof expected for CRSession failures.

options.title: Accept a narrow classifier
options.body: Add a narrowly proven Playwright CRSession assertion classifier that suppresses only this dependency shape and preserves generic unhandled-rejection fatal behavior.

options.title: Wait for fresh live repro
options.body: Do not implement until a current-main raw or remote CDP scenario reproduces the CRSession._onMessage assertion with logs.

recommendation.title: Design browser recovery boundary first
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open while a browser/Gateway owner defines profile quarantine or subprocess isolation semantics and the live proof expected for CRSession failures.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest combined history across the central unhandled-rejection handler and bundled browser Playwright CDP ownership boundary.
